sections.h2: Which two offices deal with property tax in McCreary County?
sections.html:
The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) fixes the value, and the Sheriff receives the payment. That split holds statewide, but McCreary County adds a twist: with no incorporated city anywhere inside its lines, there is no city hall tax office and no city levy. County government is the one local government covering every resident.

Mail for the PVA goes to PO Box 609, Whitley City, KY 42653, with a telephone line at (606) 376-2514 and a fax line at (606) 376-4152. Dial (606) 376-2322 for the Sheriff and (606) 376-2411 for the County Clerk, the office that records deeds and inherits bills nobody paid. The fiscal court works from 1 North Main Street in Whitley City and opens its monthly public meeting at 6 p.m. on second Thursdays.

sections.h2: When do penalties begin on a McCreary County bill?
sections.html:
Under KRS 134.015 the value is fixed as of January 1, the bill is due by the last day of the year, and the Sheriff accepts money until April 15. Delay costs more at each step:

  • Full payment by November 1 trims 2 percent.
  • From November 2 to New Year's Eve, the printed total applies.
  • January adds a 5 percent surcharge.
  • Past January the surcharge is 10 percent.

November 1, 2026 has come and gone, so a 2026 bill carries the printed figure through December 31 and a penalty afterward. The County Clerk inherits anything unpaid when April 15 ends. Two mailed warnings from the county attorney follow, then a sale scheduled three to four and a half months after the transfer. Whoever buys the certificate may add charges, so settle with the Sheriff first.

sections.h2: What does a McCreary County house cost in tax?
sections.html:
Very little, by Kentucky standards, because values here are low. Census puts a typical owned home at $85,300, against $188,100 in McCracken County. Frankfort's 2025 rate, 10.6 cents per $100, yields about $90.42 for the state on that house. More comes from the county, the school board and any special district, and the PVA can add them up for one address.

With zero permits in 2025, the roll gains little from new building, and the market is existing houses. The 2020 census listed 6,892 housing units, 12.1 percent of them vacant, and 17.9 percent of residents today are 65 or older.

sections.h2: Does McCreary County offer a homestead deduction?
sections.html:
Yes, since the exemption is a state program. Homeowners 65 or older, and those classed as totally disabled, get $49,100 subtracted from assessed value for 2025 and 2026 before rates are applied.

The subtraction bites hard in this county. At the $85,300 median, only $36,200 stays taxable, and the state's piece drops from about $90.42 to about $38.37. File at the PVA office in Whitley City and prove age with a birth certificate, driver's license or passport. Disability claims need a federal or retirement-system finding of total disability and yearly renewal, with exceptions for service-connected veterans and for people ruled totally and permanently disabled by Social Security or the Kentucky Retirement Systems.

sections.h2: What can a McCreary County owner do about an assessment?
sections.html:
Ask for a meeting with the PVA or a deputy before anything else. Kentucky refuses appeals from owners who skipped it. The PVA must explain how the number was produced, and then the steps run:

  • Review the roll in the 13-day window that starts the first Monday in May.
  • Lodge the appeal with the County Clerk by the end of the first working day after that window.
  • Attach evidence on land and structures: insurance records, build costs, comparable sales and photographs. A survey helps with rural tracts. Unsupported appeals fail.
  • Appear before the local board, which convenes a month or so after viewing ends and takes evidence only with both sides present.

An owner who misses the hearing loses the next step, the Kentucky Claims Commission. And when the board lands above your claim after bills have printed, you receive a supplemental bill.

sections.h2: What if McCreary County taxes are still owed when the house sells?
sections.html:
The debt rides along with the parcel. The statute treats these taxes as the owner's own debt from the assessment date, and a lien under KRS 134.420 can persist 11 years whoever holds title. At the Clerk's office, interest of 1 percent per month starts, commissions are added for both the Clerk and the county attorney, and so is a recording fee.

Title companies want a payoff figure before they release funds. Get it from the Sheriff up to April 15, and from the Clerk afterward.

sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in McCreary County?
sections.html:
The newest of Kentucky's 120 counties, McCreary was cut from Pulaski, Wayne and Whitley in 1912. It spans 431 square miles on the Cumberland Plateau's western rim, and no part of it lies inside an incorporated city, which no other Kentucky county can say. Whitley City is the seat, with Pine Knot and Stearns as the other census-designated places. Federal land dominates the map: about 43 percent sits in the Daniel Boone National Forest and 18 percent in the Big South Fork National River and Recreation Area, so private acreage is a limited share.

Early livelihoods came from timber, coal and the Cincinnati Southern Railway, which arrived in 1880 and fed the Stearns company town. Cumberland Falls, which joined the state park system in 1930, and the Big South Fork Scenic Railway draw visitors now. Students all attend the McCreary County School District, and McCreary Central is its comprehensive high school. Clocks follow Eastern time, and the 2025 population of 17,124 is 1.4 percent above 2020.

The average worker needs 32.3 minutes to reach a job, and 80.1 percent of households have a broadband subscription. Pulaski, Laurel, Whitley and Wayne counties border it, along with two Tennessee counties. For an heir to a house here, or an owner behind on tax, an as-is cash sale avoids paying for repairs first. The sale price still has to clear the tax payoff, so get that number early.

Population peaked at 18,306 in 2010, and the 2020 count of 16,888 was a 7.7 percent drop. Census business data list 157 employer establishments with 1,522 jobs in 2023, down 4.3 percent from the year before, and retail sales near $110 million in 2022. Only 8.5 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree, and 18.8 percent of residents under 65 live with a disability. Those figures describe a market of local buyers and heirs more than of relocating workers, so pricing near the county's low median value matters.

faqs.q: Is there a city property tax in McCreary County?
faqs.a: No. McCreary is the only Kentucky county without an incorporated city, so no city levy exists. School and district levies still appear on the bill.

faqs.q: Whom do I pay for McCreary County property tax?
faqs.a: The Sheriff, at (606) 376-2322, takes payment until April 15. The PVA at (606) 376-2514 sets values and receives exemption papers, never money.

faqs.q: How much state tax does an $85,300 McCreary County home owe?
faqs.a: About $90.42, using the 2025 state rate of 10.6 cents per $100. Local rates are charged in addition.

faqs.q: Can a 65-year-old in McCreary County shrink the taxable value?
faqs.a: Yes. Take proof of age to the PVA office, and the homestead deduction removes $49,100 from assessed value for 2025 and 2026.

faqs.q: What if my McCreary County bill moves to the County Clerk?
faqs.a: Expect a recorded lien and interest at 1 percent monthly. A sale of the certificate to an investor can happen 90 to 135 days later.
